text:
sanjay: Heads-up — thinking about consolidating attribute fingerprint and cost-signature flow. Current state: multiple headers (`x-rd-attr`, `x-rd-billing`, `x-provenance`) and two late-join lookup paths. We get duplication in ingest and weird attribution gaps.

mia: +1. Can we pick one canonical header for propagation and have a migration shim? The late-join lookup is expensive in the hot path.

elaine: Agreed. Biggest constraints: 1) must work for edge proxies where we only see compressed headers, 2) backwards compat for older SDKs, 3) minimal added header size (cost).

chris: Proposal sketch: one compact header `x-rd-costsig` that encodes minimal attribution keys (tenant, route, optional cohort) with a version prefix. Fast path: decode at gateway. Fallback: if missing, do current lookup.

sanjay: Example payload:
```json
{"v":"1","t":"acct:42","r":"/generate","c":"cohort-A","s":"hmac:abcd..."}
```
We keep HMAC for tamper detection. Gateway can strip and stash into envelope; downstream services read it from envelope rather than doing DB lookups.

mia: How big is that in practice? We should quantify header length and worst-case token overhead (gzipped/encoded in proxy).

chris: Rough numbers: base64 hmac ~44 bytes, rest ~<60 bytes => ~100 bytes header. With compression and HTTP/2 overhead it's small compared to payloads. But if many headers per request it adds up.

elaine: Migration plan idea: 1) implement gateway encoder/decoder, 2) opt-in flag on SDK to write `x-rd-costsig`, 3) roll forward ingest to prefer `x-rd-costsig` then fallback to existing enrichment. 4) measure mismatch rate and roll through.

sanjay: Operational concerns: key rotation for HMAC, what happens when signature fails? Fail open (accept and mark untrusted) vs fail closed (do lookup). I vote fail open but metric-tagged.

elaine: +1 fail-open with a `costsig.trust` boolean attached to envelope. That way billing teams can filter untrusted at rollup time.

mia: Also need a small shim for long-tail proxies that only allow limited header sets (some customers). Maybe allow embedding into a small cookie or the first bytes of an existing `x-rd-attr` key. Not ideal but pragmatic.

chris: For implementation: minimal decoder in gateway (Go) + a tiny library in runtime clients (TS/Python/Go) that encodes. Also a compatibility transform in the ingress lambda for private deployments.

sanjay: Can we standardize the JSON schema now? Suggest fields: v, t (tenant), r (route hash), c (cohort), s (sig), m (metadata kv compressed). Keep schema stable.

elaine: One more thing: how do we handle sampling? If sampled traces drop the header, we should still propagate cost sig separately. I propose copying `x-rd-costsig` into envelope before any sampler drops payload.

mia: Action items: 
- chris: prototype encoder/decoder + size bench (this week)
- elaine: write migration rollout doc + trust semantics (ETA Tue)
- sanjay: sketch metrics to track mismatch and fail-open rates

chris: acked. I'll post PR with bench numbers and a toy shim for the gateway.

ingest-bot: deploy-check: gateway-decoder-proto (ci/build) — all tests passed :white_check_mark:

sanjay: Thanks all. If chris' numbers look good we'll open an RFC for the header schema and migration timeline.

mia: One tiny UX ask: add an observability tag `costsig.source=gateway|sdk|ingest-lookup` so we can roll up attribution accuracy by source.

elaine: noted. We'll include that in the rollout doc.

chris: PR link: https://git.redwood/eng/gateway/pulls/428 — bench + sample encoder (WIP).

sanjay: perfect — let's sync at next eng-platform weekly if anything surprising pops up. :thumbsup:
